sections.heading: A backup plan turns the RPO and the retention into scheduled rules

plan.problem: A company must lose at most one day of data and keep monthly backups for years. Four services in several accounts must follow the same rule.
trace: **Set the objective.** The RPO is the [maximum acceptable amount of time since the last data recovery point] (well-architected-rpo-definition); the RTO is the [maximum acceptable delay between the interruption of service and restoration of service] (well-architected-rto-definition). How often you back up decides the RPO you can meet.

**Write the rules.** A backup plan is the [central data protection policy called a backup plan] (backup-faq-backup-plan-central-policy), [comprised of one or more backup rules] (backup-faq-backup-rule-four-parts): a schedule, a backup window, a lifecycle and a target backup vault. [Backup jobs are started within this window] (backup-window-jobs-start-within-window).
**Select resources.** AWS Backup can [apply backup plans to your AWS resources] by their tags (backup-plan-applied-by-tagging-resources).

**Pass a role.** For each resource assignment [you must pass a service role] that AWS Backup uses to [create, tag, and delete resources in your account] (backup-iam-role-passed-for-plans-on-demand-copy-restore).
plan.trace_note: Keep the service opt-in out of the trace: it is the Stop and answer. Bold backup plan, backup rule, backup window and resource assignment at first use (term requests).
plan.table: Where the plan lives (columns: Question | Backup plan in one account | Backup policy in AWS Organizations): Who edits it | the account itself | the management account or a delegated administrator ([Manage backup policies across accounts in AWS Organizations], backup-delegated-admin-privileges-manage-policies-row, or write the cell without a link); What member accounts see | their own plan | [a corresponding backup plan] that is [visible in that account] (backup-org-policy-creates-visible-plan-in-each-account), [as an immutable plan for that account] (organizations-backup-policy-effective-plan-immutable); How it selects resources | tags or resource ARNs | [by resource types] or tags, [not by individual resource ARNs] (backup-org-policy-resources-by-type-or-tag-not-arns). Three rows; cells at most 15 words; link each fact once in the subsection.
plan.why: Why rules, not scripts? A rule says what you want (how often, how long, where), and AWS Backup [automates the creation of backups] (backup-faq-assigned-resources-encrypted-vault). When two rules run on the same day, AWS Backup keeps the backup under the [rule with the longer retention period] (backup-overlapping-rules-longer-retention-wins).
plan.exam_signal: "one backup policy for all accounts in the organization" points to backup policies in AWS Organizations, which [centrally manage and apply backup plans] (organizations-backup-policy-effective-plan-immutable); "take a backup now, outside the schedule" points to an on-demand backup, which [begins to back up your resource immediately] (backup-on-demand-backup-starts-immediately).

A delegated administrator lets assigned users work [outside the management account] (backup-delegated-admin-performs-most-admin-tasks-from-member-account), but the [resource opt-in settings in the management account override] those of member accounts (backup-org-management-account-opt-in-overrides-member-accounts). Each member account needs a vault and [the IAM role that will be used] (backup-org-member-accounts-need-vault-and-iam-role).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: write the RPO and the retention as rules in one backup plan. The thing to watch is the role that AWS Backup uses in each account.

sections.heading: Each backup becomes a recovery point in an encrypted backup vault

plan.problem: A backup job finishes. The team wants to know where the backup lives, what it stores, and which key protects it.
trace: **Store.** AWS Backup [saves recovery points in backup vaults] (backup-recovery-points-saved-in-vaults); a recovery point [represents the content of a resource] at a specified time (backup-recovery-point-is-backup-at-specified-time).

**Store less.** For supported resource types the first backup [backs up a full copy of your data] and later backups store [only the changes to your AWS resources] (backup-incremental-first-full-then-changes); each one keeps the [reference data to allow a full restore] (backup-incremental-restore-full-even-after-first-backup-expired).

**Encrypt.** The vault key [applies to the backups of certain resource types]; the other backups keep the key [used to encrypt the source resource] (backup-vault-key-applies-only-to-independent-encryption-types).

**Keep apart.** Backups are stored [across multiple Availability Zones] (backup-resilience-stored-across-azs-eleven-nines), and a vault keeps EC2 and EBS backups [even if you delete the source Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon EBS volumes] (backup-vault-backups-immutable-content-and-survive-source-deletion).
plan.trace_note: Bold recovery point, backup vault and incremental backup at first use. The 11 nines number goes to the B-list only.
plan.table: Which key encrypts the backup (columns: Resource | Backup encrypted with | Independent encryption): Amazon EFS | the key of the backup vault: [Amazon EFS backups are always encrypted] (backup-encryption-efs-row) | yes; Amazon S3 | the vault key, [even if the source Amazon S3 buckets are not encrypted] (backup-encryption-s3-row) | yes; Amazon EBS | the key [used to encrypt the source volume] (backup-encryption-ebs-row) | no; Amazon RDS | the key used to [encrypt the source Amazon RDS database] (backup-encryption-rds-row) | no. Four rows; the 'yes' and 'no' cells need no link.

For resource types with full AWS Backup management the backup belongs to AWS Backup ([Backup ARNs begin with] arn:aws:backup, backup-full-management-backup-arns-for-backup-specific-policies); for the others the relation to the service's own backups [varies by service] (backup-native-relationship-varies-by-service), and the snapshot keeps the encryption of its source.

sections.heading: Continuous backups allow point-in-time restore but keep at most 35 days

plan.problem: A bad deployment corrupts a database at 10:20. The last daily backup is from midnight, so restoring it loses a morning of orders. The team wants the state of 10:19.

**Record.** AWS Backup takes a full backup and then keeps [constantly backing up your resource's transaction logs] (backup-pitr-continuous-works-by-full-backup-and-transaction-logs).
**Rewind.** A restore goes to the time you choose, [within 1 second of precision], back [a maximum of 35 days] (backup-pitr-restore-rewinds-to-chosen-time).
**Know the edge.** Amazon RDS restores up to the [most recent 5 minutes of activity], Amazon S3 up to the [most recent 15 minutes of activity] (backup-pitr-latest-restorable-time-by-service).
plan.trace_note: The problem's times (10:20, 10:19, midnight) are story data of the problem sentence; keep them out of the trace. plan.why: Why does AWS recommend [both continuous and snapshot backup rules] (backup-pitr-recommend-continuous-and-snapshot-rules-together)? The continuous rule gives the exact second for a recent mistake; the snapshot rule keeps the long history that a continuous backup cannot keep.
plan.exam_signal: "undo accidental deletions in an S3 bucket" points to continuous S3 backups, which help with [undoing accidental deletions]; "long-term retention" points to periodic backups, which serve [long-term data retention needs] (backup-faq-s3-continuous-vs-periodic-use).

End with <!-- trap: backup-trap-copy-keeps-pitr -->. At most 40 words.

sections.heading: The lifecycle moves some backups to cold storage and later deletes them

plan.problem: Monthly backups must stay for years. Keeping all of them in the normal storage tier costs money every month, and most of them will never be restored.
trace: **Start warm.** Every backup is first [stored in warm storage]; the lifecycle can later move it to a [lower-cost tier called cold storage] (backup-every-backup-starts-in-warm-storage).

**Check the type.** Cold storage exists for, among others, [Amazon EBS (using EBS Snapshot Archive)], [Amazon EFS] and [DynamoDB with advanced features] (backup-cold-storage-resource-types); for other types the setting is [ignored for other resources] (backup-cold-storage-ignored-for-unsupported-resources).

**Stay long enough.** A backup stays in cold storage for a [minimum of 90 days] (backup-cold-storage-min-90-days-retention-rule); deleting it earlier costs a [pro-rated charge equal to the storage charge] (backup-pricing-cold-early-deletion-prorated-90-days).
**Expire.** At the end of the lifecycle, AWS Backup deletes the backup at a random point [over the following 8 hours] (backup-plan-expired-backups-deleted-within-8-hours).
plan.trace_note: Bold lifecycle, warm storage and cold storage at first use. The lifecycle timeline backup-lifecycle (optional, see diagrams) goes after the trace only if words remain.

(columns: Resource | Cold storage | Note): Amazon EBS | yes | when backups run [monthly or less often] (backup-cold-ebs-is-snapshot-archive-monthly-or-less); Amazon EFS | yes | (empty or a dash); Amazon DynamoDB | with advanced features | the plain row has no lifecycle check (backup-feature-row-dynamodb), the advanced row has one ([DynamoDB with AWS Backup advanced features], backup-feature-row-dynamodb-advanced); Amazon Aurora | no | no check mark for lifecycle in the feature table for [Amazon Aurora] (backup-feature-row-aurora); Amazon S3 | no | [Cold storage transition of S3 backups is not supported] (backup-s3-no-cold-storage-transition). sections.heading: A copy in another Region or account survives the loss of the source

plan.problem: All backups sit in one account and one Region. If the Region fails, or someone deletes backups in that account, nothing is left to restore.
trace: **Add a copy action.** A rule can copy each backup [in the same or another AWS Region], [in the same account or another account] (backup-copy-action-same-or-other-region-and-account), [on demand or automatically] (backup-cross-region-copy-on-demand-or-scheduled).

**Copy to a Region.** The first copy to a new Region [copies the backup in full]; later copies [in the same AWS Region will be incremental] (backup-cross-region-first-copy-full-then-incremental). The copy uses [the KMS key of the target vault] (backup-encryption-copy-uses-destination-vault-key).

**Copy to an account.** The accounts [must belong to the same organization] (backup-cross-account-requires-same-organization); the [management account] turns on cross-account backup (backup-cross-account-management-account-enables-feature); the destination vault allows [the access policy backup:CopyIntoBackupVault] (backup-cross-account-destination-vault-must-allow-copy-into).

**Recover.** If the original is [inadvertently deleted], you copy it back [from its destination account to its source account] and restore it (backup-cross-account-copy-purpose-recover-deleted-original).

sections.heading: Vault Lock in compliance mode stops even the root user from deleting backups

plan.problem: An administrator's credentials are stolen. IAM permissions cannot stop someone who already holds every permission in the account.
trace: **Choose a mode.** AWS Backup Vault Lock has [Governance mode] and [Compliance mode] (backup-vault-lock-two-modes-governance-compliance).
**Set retention limits.** The lock sets a minimum and a maximum retention; new backup and copy jobs [will fail if they do not conform] (backup-vault-lock-min-max-retention-fail-nonconforming-jobs).

**Wait out the grace time.** A compliance lock has a grace time of [at least 3 days (72 hours)] (backup-vault-lock-grace-time-minimum-3-days); after it, the lock [cannot be altered or deleted by any user] (backup-vault-lock-compliance-immutable-by-anyone).

**Deny deletes.** In a locked vault, when any user, [including the root user], tries to delete a backup or change its lifecycle, [AWS Backup will deny the operation] (backup-vault-lock-denies-delete-and-lifecycle-change-even-root).

traps.belief: A replica or standby copy of the data (Multi-AZ, a read replica, S3 replication, a global table) is a backup, so the workload needs no separate backups.
traps.truth: A copy that follows every change also receives deletes and corruption; only a recovery point keeps the content of a resource at a specified time, and even multi-site designs still need backups for data corruption.

traps.belief: Any AWS Backup Vault Lock stops every administrator from deleting backups.
traps.truth: A lock in governance mode can be removed by users with sufficient IAM permissions; only a lock in compliance mode, after its grace time, cannot be altered or deleted by any user.

traps.belief: The KMS key of a backup vault encrypts every backup stored in that vault, so an unencrypted database gets encrypted backups.
traps.truth: The vault key applies only to the backups of certain resource types (those with full AWS Backup management); EBS, RDS and Aurora backups keep the key of the source, and backups of an unencrypted RDS database stay unencrypted.

traps.belief: A cross-Region or cross-account copy of a continuous backup still allows point-in-time restore.
traps.truth: The copy becomes a snapshot (periodic) backup, and point-in-time restore is not available for it.

traps.belief: Any backup can move to cold storage to save money, whatever the resource type or rule.
traps.truth: Cold storage exists only for listed resource types and is ignored for the others (Aurora and S3 backups do not transition); continuous backups never transition, and a backup must stay at least 90 days in cold storage.

traps.belief: An AWS Backup copy action can send backups to any AWS account, including an account of another company.
traps.truth: Cross-account copies need accounts in the same organization, cross-account backup turned on by the management account and a destination vault policy that allows backup:CopyIntoBackupVault; an account outside the organization gets access through a logically air-gapped vault shared with AWS RAM.

traps.belief: A restore with AWS Backup writes the data back into the original resource and replaces what is there.
traps.truth: For most resource types AWS Backup creates a new resource during restore; an S3 restore into the original bucket skips existing objects, an EFS restore goes to a recovery directory, and only Redshift Serverless and SAP HANA on EC2 restores overwrite.

faq.question: Can a backup be kept after its retention period ends?
faq.answer: Yes, with a legal hold, kept [even if their retention period is over] (backup-faq-legal-hold-definition).

question_slots.plan: A company runs Amazon RDS, Amazon EFS, Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon EBS in many accounts of one organization in AWS Organizations. A new regulation mandates one backup policy for every account and a monthly report that shows compliance with it. LEAST operational overhead. Key: AWS Backup policies in AWS Organizations, plus an AWS Backup Audit Manager framework with a report (organizations-backup-policy-effective-plan-immutable, backup-faq-audit-manager-purpose, backup-faq-audit-manager-multi-account-reports). Distractors: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policies in each account [misconception: it automates EBS snapshots only; backup-faq-dlm-vs-backup-when-to-use]; an AWS Lambda function on an EventBridge schedule in each account that creates snapshots and writes a report [how-the-exam-asks-trap-works-means-correct]; the backup settings of each service plus AWS Config rules that check them [misconception: backups made outside AWS Backup are not centrally governed; backup-native-service-backups-not-centrally-governed; how-the-exam-asks-trap-detect-meets-ensure only if the text states detection as the solution].

Shared context with q006: a company stores the backups of its databases in one AWS Backup vault and must keep each backup for its full retention period. Changed phrase (the only difference from q006): 'No user, including the root user, can delete a backup or shorten its retention before the retention period ends.' Ask 'Which solution will meet these requirements?'. Options identical in q002 and q006, in neutral words: (a) turn on AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode with a grace time, and let the grace time expire [key here; backup-vault-lock-compliance-immutable-by-anyone, backup-vault-lock-denies-delete-and-lifecycle-change-even-root]; (b) turn on AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode [trap backup-trap-governance-stops-admins; key in q006]; (c) turn on S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for the backup vault [misconception: Object Lock protects object versions in S3 buckets, not backup vaults; s3-faq-object-lock-what; impossible-feature]; (d) turn on the AWS Backup Audit Manager control that checks whether vaults prevent manual deletion of recovery points [how-the-exam-asks-trap-detect-meets-ensure; backup-audit-manager-control-vault-prevent-deletion]. Facts: backup-vault-lock-compliance-immutable-by-anyone, backup-vault-lock-governance-lock-removable-with-iam, backup-vault-lock-two-modes-governance-compliance.

A company backs up Amazon EBS volumes and Amazon EFS file systems with one AWS Backup plan. Daily backups must be retained for 30 days; monthly backups must be retained for 7 years and are infrequently accessed. MOST cost-effective. Key: in the monthly rule, add a lifecycle that transitions the backups to cold storage and expires them after 7 years; leave the daily rule in warm storage (backup-cold-storage-resource-types, backup-cold-ebs-is-snapshot-archive-monthly-or-less, backup-cold-storage-min-90-days-retention-rule). Distractors: transition the backups of the daily rule to cold storage after 1 day [backup-trap-every-backup-goes-cold; backup-cold-storage-plan-total-retention-90-days, ebs-archive-recommended-monthly-not-daily]; copy the monthly backups into an S3 bucket and transition them to S3 Glacier Deep Archive with an S3 Lifecycle rule [ebs-trap-snapshots-in-my-s3-bucket; ebs-snapshot-s3-buckets-not-accessible]; transition the monthly backups to cold storage and copy them to a second Region every month [different-problem and impossible: backup-copy-cold-storage-backups-cannot-be-copied].

Shared context with q009: a company protects an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with AWS Backup. Changed phrase (the only difference from q009): 'The company must be able to restore the database to its state of a few minutes before an error, for errors found within the last 2 weeks.' Options identical in q004 and q009: (a) a backup rule with continuous backups turned on and a retention of 14 days [key here; backup-continuous-rule-allows-pitr-unlike-snapshot, backup-retention-continuous-range, backup-pitr-latest-restorable-time-by-service]; (b) a backup rule that creates a snapshot backup on the first day of every month with a retention of 5 years [key in q009; here it cannot reach a point minutes before an error]; (c) a backup rule with continuous backups turned on and a lifecycle that transitions them to cold storage after 30 days [impossible-feature: backup-pitr-no-cold-storage-because-35-vs-90]; (d) a continuous backup rule with a copy action to a second Region, and point-in-time restores from the copy [trap backup-trap-copy-keeps-pitr; backup-continuous-copy-becomes-snapshot-no-pitr]. The twin line of each question quotes the changed phrase of the other.

(Select TWO.) A company uses AWS Backup in its organization in AWS Organizations. A recovery partner, whose AWS account belongs to a different organization, must be able to restore the company's backups if the company's accounts are compromised. The backups must stay isolated from the company's production accounts. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Keys: (1) create a logically air-gapped vault and copy the backups to it (backup-lag-vault-definition-secondary-vault-rto, backup-lag-vault-encryption-key-and-compliance-lock); (2) share the logically air-gapped vault with the partner's account ID through AWS RAM (backup-faq-lag-vault-share-ram, backup-lag-vault-share-with-account-ids-only, backup-lag-vault-restore-from-owner-or-shared-account). Distractors: add a copy action that copies the backups directly into a vault in the partner's account [trap backup-trap-cross-account-any-account; backup-cross-account-requires-same-organization]; share the standard backup vault with the partner through AWS RAM [misconception: backup-lag-vs-standard-sharing-row, a standard vault is not compatible with AWS RAM]; share the EBS snapshots publicly so that the partner can copy them [violates the isolation requirement; ebs-snapshot-only-unencrypted-public]. Five options. Do not key on multi-party approval (volatile).

Same context and same four options as q002. Changed phrase: 'Most users must not be able to delete a backup or shorten its retention, but members of the security team who hold a specific IAM permission must be able to remove the protection.' Key moves to (b) governance mode (backup-vault-lock-governance-lock-removable-with-iam, backup-vault-lock-governance-intent-designated-personnel). Option (a), compliance mode, now fails the requirement, because after the grace time the lock [cannot be altered or deleted by any user] (backup-vault-lock-compliance-immutable-by-anyone): distractor_type violates-requirement, with a misconception sentence. Options (c) and (d) keep their traps. The twin line of each question quotes the changed phrase of the other.

A company backs up an unencrypted Amazon RDS DB instance with AWS Backup. A new rule mandates that every backup is encrypted at rest with a customer managed KMS key. Which solution meets this requirement? Key: take a DB snapshot, copy it with encryption under the customer managed key, restore a new encrypted DB instance from the copy, and back up the new instance (rds-encrypt-existing-via-snapshot-copy, backup-encryption-rds-row). Distractors: create a new backup vault that uses the customer managed key and send the backups there [trap backup-trap-vault-key-encrypts-everything; backup-vault-key-applies-only-to-independent-encryption-types]; modify the DB instance to turn on encryption with the customer managed key [rds-trap-encrypt-existing-in-place; rds-encryption-only-at-create]; turn on the AWS Backup Audit Manager control 'Recovery points are encrypted' [how-the-exam-asks-trap-detect-meets-ensure; backup-audit-manager-control-encrypted]. Do not use a cross-Region or cross-account copy as an option: backup-encryption-copy-uses-destination-vault-key makes it ambiguous.

A company runs an internal reporting application with an Amazon RDS database in one AWS Region. If the Region fails, the business finds it acceptable to recover within a day and to lose up to a day of data. The company wants the MOST cost-effective disaster recovery solution. Key: daily AWS Backup backups with a copy action to a backup vault in a second Region; restore there only after a disaster (backup-copy-action-same-or-other-region-and-account, backup-resilience-copy-across-regions-greater-resilience, well-architected-rpo-definition, well-architected-rto-definition). Distractors: a pilot light with a cross-Region read replica that runs all the time [violates-qualifier; aurora-cmp-wp-pilot-light-core-infrastructure-always-available; how-the-exam-asks-trap-always-max-availability]; a warm standby with a scaled-down copy of the application in the second Region [violates-qualifier; aurora-cmp-wp-warm-standby-faster-than-pilot-light]; a Multi-AZ deployment in the same Region [how-the-exam-asks-trap-multi-az-covers-region]. The stem's 'within a day' and 'a day of data' are requirements, not AWS numbers. Do not state in the explanation that backup and restore is the lowest-cost strategy as an AWS fact (the Well-Architected fact is not verified); argue from the always-on resources of the other options.

Same context and same four options as q004. Changed phrase: 'The company must keep a restorable backup of the database from the end of every month for 5 years.' Key moves to (b) the monthly snapshot rule with a 5-year retention (backup-retention-snapshot-range, backup-snapshot-hourly-and-100-years). Option (a), the continuous rule, now fails, because continuous backups keep [1 day to 35 days] (backup-retention-continuous-range): misconception sentence 'a continuous backup can be kept for years' (rds-trap-retention-beyond-35-days only if the text states that belief). Options (c) and (d) keep their traps.

A company stores orders in an Amazon DynamoDB global table with replicas in two AWS Regions. A faulty deployment overwrote many items. The company must be able to recover the table to its state before such a change. Key: turn on point-in-time recovery for the table (dynamodb-pitr-protects-accidental-writes-deletes, dynamodb-pitr-35-days-default-1-to-35-configurable), or AWS Backup periodic backups (backup-faq-recovery-point-definition); write one key only. Distractors: fail over to the replica in the second Region [trap backup-trap-replication-is-backup; dynamodb-trap-backup-is-standby]; add a replica in a third Region [backup-trap-replication-is-backup, different wording]; turn on DynamoDB Streams to keep the changes [misconception; dynamodb-trap-stream-keeps-changes only if the text states that belief]. Difficulty 1: qualifier none is allowed.

(Select TWO.) A company uses AWS Backup. Auditors require monthly evidence that backups can be restored and that each restore finishes within a target time. LEAST operational overhead. Keys: (1) a restore testing plan that restores recovery points on a schedule (backup-restore-testing-automated-periodic-evaluation, backup-restore-testing-plan-steps); (2) an AWS Backup Audit Manager framework with the control 'Restore time for resources meet target' and a report plan (backup-audit-manager-control-restore-time, backup-audit-manager-frameworks-and-daily-reports). Distractors: an engineer restores one backup by hand each month and records the time in a spreadsheet [violates-qualifier; how-the-exam-asks-trap-works-means-correct]; AWS CloudTrail logs of the backup jobs [misconception: shows that backups ran, not that restores work; backup-faq-cloudtrail-activity-logs]; Vault Lock in compliance mode [how-the-exam-asks-trap-keyword-bait]. speak.prompt: If an attacker gets administrator access in production, can the attacker delete our backups?

plan.ten_second: Not if the backup vault is locked in compliance mode and a copy sits in a separate account. Governance mode alone does not stop an administrator.
key_points_must: In a locked vault, AWS Backup denies deletes and lifecycle changes, even from the root user (backup-vault-lock-denies-delete-and-lifecycle-change-even-root).
After the grace time, a compliance-mode lock cannot be altered or deleted by any user (backup-vault-lock-compliance-immutable-by-anyone).
A governance-mode lock can be removed by users with sufficient IAM permissions (backup-vault-lock-governance-lock-removable-with-iam).
A copy in another account of the organization lets you copy a deleted backup back and restore it (backup-cross-account-copy-purpose-recover-deleted-original).

cards.front: In AWS Backup, a continuous backup can be kept for {{c1::1 day to 35 days}}.

cards.back: No: the copy is a snapshot backup
